evals.description: wuauserv StartType Disabled blocks patch baseline; skill must re-enable (Set-Service Automatic) not just start, and note a GPO may re-disable it.
evals.prompt: On a Windows Server 2019 EC2 instance, AWS-RunPatchBaseline fails with 0x80070422 'The service cannot be started' and Get-Service wuauserv shows StartType: Disabled. Why can't SSM just start it, and how do I fix it?
evals.expected_output: Explains that SSM / the patch baseline can start a Stopped or Manual service but cannot start a Disabled one, which is why it fails with 0x80070422. The fix is to re-enable it with Set-Service -Name wuauserv -StartupType Automatic, then Start-Service, and also check BITS isn't Disabled. Notes that if a GPO set it Disabled it will revert on the next policy refresh (~90 min), so the GPO must be fixed for a durable solution, and to get approval if it was disabled intentionally.
assertions: Explains that a Disabled service cannot be started by SSM until its StartType is changed (unlike Stopped/Manual)
Recommends Set-Service -StartupType Automatic then starting the service
Notes a GPO may re-disable the service on the next refresh

evals.description: WUA scan hangs with svchost pegged; skill should reset services and, for a corrupt scan DB, rebuild SoftwareDistribution/DataStore.edb.
evals.prompt: A Windows Server 2016 EC2 instance never returns from a patch scan. wuauserv is stuck 'Stopping', TiWorker and svchost are pegged at ~100% CPU for over an hour, and DataStore.edb is over 1GB. How do I get the scan working again?
evals.expected_output: Explains this is a hung WUA with a likely-corrupt scan database. The fix is to stop wuauserv and BITS, kill the hung TiWorker/wuauclt processes, and reset the update state — rename/clear SoftwareDistribution (which rebuilds DataStore.edb on the next scan), optionally re-register the WUA DLLs, then restart the services and confirm a search succeeds. Notes that if it doesn't hold, an outdated SSU / CBS store corruption may be the underlying cause.
assertions: Recommends stopping the services and resetting SoftwareDistribution / rebuilding DataStore.edb for the corrupt scan database
Recommends killing the hung TiWorker/wuauclt processes
Notes a stale SSU or CBS store corruption as a possible underlying cause if the reset doesn't hold

evals.description: AWS-RunPatchBaseline throws a type-load error for AWSSDK.Core; skill must recognize a GAC-missing assembly and re-register with gacutil.
evals.prompt: On a Windows Server 2019 EC2 instance, AWS-RunPatchBaseline fails immediately with "Invoke-PatchBaselineOperation : Could not load type 'Amazon.Runtime.Internal.InvokeOptions' from assembly 'AWSSDK.Core'". The OS itself patches fine manually. What is wrong and how do I fix it?
evals.expected_output: Identifies that the AWSSDK.Core .NET assembly is missing or corrupt in the Global Assembly Cache (GAC), so AWS-RunPatchBaseline (which loads AWS SDK types) cannot run — even though the OS patches fine manually. The fix is to locate AWSSDK.Core.dll (under the AWS SDK for .NET install) and re-register it into the GAC with gacutil /i (after taking an EBS snapshot), then verify the assembly loads and the InvokeOptions type resolves, and re-run the baseline scan. Notes excluding the SDK path from AV to prevent recurrence.
assertions: Identifies AWSSDK.Core missing/corrupt in the GAC as the cause of the AWS-RunPatchBaseline type-load error
Recommends re-registering AWSSDK.Core.dll into the GAC with gacutil /i
Distinguishes this AWS-RunPatchBaseline runtime failure from a normal Windows Update problem
